notes: Direct HTTP fetch (tier 1) for homepage/robots/sitemaps; Playwright (tier 2) to render the client-side Unbxd product count on the badge-collection URL (raw HTML does not embed the count for this page type). No bot protection, no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow. Top nav has no persistent 'New Arrivals'/'New In' department tab (only Bedroom/Decor/Kitchen/Furnishings/Tableware/Gifting/Sale). Found a homepage banner section whose own alt-text/data-ga-bannertitle is literally 'New arrivals: in stock & ready to ship', linking to https://www.homecentre.in/in/en/search?q=badge.invisible%3A279Z. This is the same '?q=badge...' URL shape this project has previously documented as a benign false-positive class on Home Centre's UAE storefront (genuine backend-matched/tagged collections, not literal free-text search) - confirmed present on the India storefront too, so it was NOT excluded by the generic suspect-search-URL heuristic, per this task's standing instruction. Opened and validated it: page's own embedded search-index JSON reports numberOfProducts:62 and the rendered page text reads ': 62 products available'; sampled 48 unique product links visible on load, all part of a real new 'Nesta Eartha' bamboo product line spanning multiple categories (Kitchenware chopping boards, Cutlery spoon rests, Kitchen storage organisers, Cooking tools) - consistent with a genuine newly-launched, in-stock product set, not an arbitrary filter. Recorded as the single New Arrivals row (qty=62, exact, from the site's own count). Also found a separate homepage carousel titled 'Homeware New Launches' with ~9 rotating banners, each linking to a DIFFERENT badge-tagged sub-collection with its own exact count (badge 519Z=28 products / a 'Mineral' branded homeware line; badge 202Z=41 / an 'Artistry' canvas-print line; badge 203Z=25 / an 'Alpana' figurines line; badges 204Z-209Z unopened) - investigated but EXCLUDED from rows: the carousel has no canonical single URL of its own (enableShopAllButton is false in its config and its header link points back to the homepage), and every individual banner shares the exact same generic alt text 'Homeware New Launches' with no distinct site-given name per sub-collection, so recording separate rows for each would mean inventing sub-category names the site itself never uses, which the brief prohibits. Checked literal site search for 'new arrivals' and 'new in' (plain free-text query, not a badge tag): Unbxd fuzzy-matched 187 products - excluded as a generic search-results page per the brief (this is ordinary keyword matching, not the exempted backend badge-collection pattern, and 'search-results pages' are explicitly excluded regardless). Sitemaps (decor/livingroom/kitchen/bedroom/diningroom/toppages.xml) grepped for new-arrival/new-in/just-in/latest slugs - 0 hits (remaining department sitemaps hit HTTP 429 on /sitemap/* and were not retried per the no-backoff-loop rule; the sampled category-URL naming scheme never encodes merchandising concepts into slugs, so this is not expected to change the conclusion).
